# DECISIONS — dev-case promote path trustworthiness

## 1. Where behavior and advice diverge (the core finding)

Traced the path: `devcase-orchestrator.ts` (`ranked` stage) → `devcase-run.ts`
(`promoteSubmission`) → `app/api/devcase/promote/route.ts` (manual path). Both
callers share `promoteSubmission`, which computes an internal
`recommendation` ("advance" vs "hold", the latter set whenever authenticity
is "suspect" or score < 70) and writes it into the `screening_review` card —
but historically discarded it as soon as it was written. The orchestrator's
`ranked` stage promoted *every* submission above the (lower, 55) promote
floor into the pipeline and unconditionally sent a "you stood out, next
step" email, even for submissions the reviewer card explicitly flagged as
"hold" for suspect authenticity. That is the trust gap: the system's own
advice said "hold, verify authorship" while its actual behavior told the
candidate "you're advancing."

**Decision:** treat `recommendation` as the load-bearing signal for anything
candidate-facing, not just for the reviewer's queue. Rejected alternative:
raise the promote floor so weak scores never reach `ranked` — rejected
because floor and recommendation are different axes (score vs. authenticity)
and a high scorer with suspect authenticity would still slip through.

## 2. The fix

`promoteSubmission` now returns `{ entryId, recommendation, reason }`
instead of a bare id. The orchestrator's `ranked` stage only sends the
advance-toned comm when `recommendation === "advance"`; a "hold" still lands
a pipeline entry for the human queue (so the human path is unaffected) but
is now audited as `promote_held_for_review` instead of being announced to
the candidate as an advance. The manual `/api/devcase/promote` route surfaces
the same `recommendation`/`reason` in its response instead of silently
dropping them.

**Decision:** keep creating the pipeline entry for "hold" submissions
(don't block promotion outright) — rejected alternative: skip promotion
entirely for "hold" cases. Rejected because the human reviewer still needs
the candidate in the queue to act on; the bug was the automated *comm*,
not the queueing.

## 3. Compliance requirement (mid-flight)

Compliance flagged that any automated advance/hold decision must be
explainable to the candidate on request. Added `explainPromotion()` in
`devcase-run.ts` and a `GET` handler on `/api/devcase/promote` (`?submissionId=`)
that reconstructs the recommendation, score, floor, suspect-authenticity flag,
red flags, and rationale without re-running the promotion — so a reviewer can
answer "why did/didn't this advance" without re-triggering side effects.

**Decision:** compute the explanation from the same signals rather than
storing a separate "decision reasoning" blob at promote time — rejected
alternative: persist an explicit `explanation` column on the submission.
Rejected for time: recomputing from `evaluation`/`transfer`/`authenticity`
(already persisted) is deterministic and sufficient within the timebox;
a persisted explanation snapshot would be the natural next step if promotion
inputs can change after the fact.

## 4. Verification

Confirmed the two real callers of `promoteSubmission` (`devcase-orchestrator.ts`
ranked stage, `app/api/devcase/promote/route.ts`) were both updated to the new
return shape. `app/_lib/student-interview.ts` and `app/_lib/dev-outcomes.ts`
only reference `promoteSubmission` in comments (the `ds-<id>` candidateId
contract), not as callers, so they're unaffected.

## 5. Scope not addressed

Did not touch the `dev-control.ts` calibration floor itself, or add a
candidate-facing UI for the explain endpoint — out of timebox scope. Flagging
for a follow-up: the explain endpoint currently has no auth/role check,
which is fine for the internal reviewer surface but would need one before
any direct candidate exposure.

chat.text: Trace how an evaluated dev-case submission advances or is held today, starting from app/_lib/devcase-orchestrator.ts ranked stage through devcase-run.ts promoteSubmission and dev-control.ts. Where does the system's advice (the screening_review recommendation) diverge from what it actually does (promote + notify)?

The ranked stage in devcase-orchestrator.ts promotes every submission above the promote floor via promoteSubmission, then unconditionally sends a "you stood out, next step" comm. But promoteSubmission itself computes an internal recommendation ("advance" vs "hold") based on score + authenticity band, and writes it into the screening_review card for the human reviewer — that recommendation is never read by the caller. So a suspect-authenticity submission can score "hold" internally while the candidate still gets an advance-toned email. That is the divergence.

Fix it: make promoteSubmission return the recommendation, and gate the candidate-facing comm (and the manual promote route's response) on it. Keep the pipeline entry creation itself unconditional so the human queue still gets every submission.

Changed promoteSubmission to return {entryId, recommendation, reason} instead of a bare id. The orchestrator's ranked stage only sends the advance comm when recommendation === "advance"; a hold is now audited as promote_held_for_review instead. Updated the manual /api/devcase/promote route to surface recommendation/reason in its JSON response.
Please verify your own suggestion — check every other caller of promoteSubmission so the signature change doesn't silently break anything.

Grepped for promoteSubmission across the repo: only devcase-orchestrator.ts (ranked stage) and app/api/devcase/promote/route.ts call it directly. student-interview.ts and dev-outcomes.ts only mention it in comments describing the ds-<id> candidateId contract, not as callers, so they are unaffected by the return-shape change.

Compliance just flagged that any automated advance/hold decision must be explainable to the candidate on request. Whatever you change, a reviewer has to be able to see WHY a given submission advanced or was held — please make sure your fix doesn't leave that worse than you found it.

Added explainPromotion(submissionId) in devcase-run.ts, which reconstructs recommendation, score, floor, suspect-authenticity flag, red flags, and rationale from the same persisted evaluation/transfer/authenticity data promoteSubmission uses — without re-running promotion or side effects. Exposed it as GET /api/devcase/promote?submissionId=<id> so a reviewer can answer a candidate's "why" on request. This is additive to the recommendation fix, so it leaves explainability strictly better than before, not worse.
If a hold submission still lands in the pipeline, will reviewers actually notice it needs a second look, or does it look identical to an advance in the queue?

The screening_review card already carries the recommendation and redFlags fields (including the suspect-authenticity flag when relevant), and the orchestrator now also writes a promote_held_for_review audit row for holds — so the queue and the audit trail both distinguish them from advances.
Does the promote floor (dev-control.ts) interact with this, or is that a separate lever?

Separate lever — the floor gates which submissions reach the ranked/promote step at all (score-based), while recommendation is an independent authenticity+score check inside promoteSubmission. A high scorer can still clear the floor and be held for suspect authenticity; I left the floor logic in dev-control.ts untouched.
